| [TERM-106](../../../record/terms.d/TERM-106.md) v4 | reconfiguration slack: the temporary resources a system needs to move between two configurations it can each hold, beyond what holding either one requires, while keeping specified commitments | A's proposal, from the pasted synthesis on constraint architectures (pasted by the owner on 2026-11-04, continuing the exchange on emergency readiness whose share link could not be fetched), Part 4. A's definition: "temporary resources required to move between otherwise feasible organizational regimes while preserving specified commitments". Made exact here as the gap between the bottleneck budget of a transition and the larger of its endpoints' holding requirements, infinite when no admissible path joins them. It folds in A's "resource-constrained reconfiguration", the name of the inquiry rather than a concept, and A's three reserves (operational, reconfiguration, competency), of which the second is what is held to meet this slack. What is held to meet it, the reconfiguration reserve, is a special case of organizational slack: measured against current output it is slack, and its use is the transition, which the output does not show. The wording is A's; adopting it is the owner's call. | Active |

| [TERM-125](../../../record/terms.d/TERM-125.md) v10 | independent execution gate, of a process: a step past which the process cannot continue unless a condition holds that its executor does not control (a person's approval, an elapsed notice period, a check another party runs or a limit another party set), whether or not the step delays it; distinct from execution impedance (added time or cost) and from an intervention opportunity (a point at which another party can bring an objection that changes the process), and not settled as a sense of procedural friction | The assistant's, offered at step 12 of the filing of the exchange "Assess Depp Heard Abuse" and accepted by the owner on 2026-11-16, renamed at the review of 2026-11-16. A gate is a step the executor cannot pass on its own. Two neighbouring properties are kept apart from it: execution impedance (does the step add time or cost?) and intervention opportunity (can another party bring an objection that changes the process?). A standing limit enforced by another's mechanism is a gate without impedance and need not be an opportunity; a rubber-stamp approval is a gate with impedance and no real opportunity; a channel for challenging a process's rules can be an opportunity without gating ordinary execution. Whether a gate is procedural friction, in the sense of the owner's claim ([CLAIM-710](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-710.md)), is left open. The wording is the assistant's (Claude, in this session); adopting it is the owner's call. | Proposed |
